- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) mid-horizon, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.8–1.2% to forecast to compensate for lagged sentiment effects.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.2 → -0.3 → +0.1), model fails to capture momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (e.g., +2%+ daily), model often fails to project sustained trend; extend upward bias by 0.3–0.7% for next 3–5 days.
